question.leadin: This politically-motivated event was perpetrated by activists who exited the Old South Meeting House dressed as Native Americans.
question.text: Name this event in which a group of rebellious colonists dumped over 300 chests of a certain British good into a Massachusetts harbor.
question.clue: The Beaver, Eleanor, and Dartmouth weren't allowed by Governor Thomas Hutchinson to return to England, leading to this event.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about famous forts in American history.
swap.text: This fort, located near Lake Champlain in New York, was captured by the Green Mountain Boys led by Ethan Allen in 1775. A popular brand of pencils also shares this name.
swap.clue: This fort's location near Lake Champlain made it useful in monitoring trade routes between New York and Canada.

question.text: de Gouges' Declaration of the Rights of Woman was a response to the Declaration of the Rights of Man, a 1789 document written in part by this French general, who had spent several years in America fighting for the colonists.
question.answerHtml: Marquis de Lafayette (accept Marie-Joseph Paul Yves Roch Gilbert du Motier)
question.clue: With the Comte de Mirabeau, this man drafted the Declaration of the Rights of Man, which was modeled after the Declaration of Independence.

swap.text: Following the Revolutionary War Battles of Germantown and Brandywine, troops retreated to this Pennsylvania encampment. Washington's army had to suffer through the harsh winter of 1777 in this location.
swap.clue: Baron von Steuben taught soldiers at this location proper bayonet training and other European drills.

question.text: This British general surrendered to American forces at the Battle of Yorktown. He later served as the military governor of Ireland.
question.clue: In another war, he served under General William Howe during the campaigns for New York City and Philadelphia, and he later defeated the army of Horatio Gates at the Battle of Camden.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about John Adams's predecessor, George Washington.
swap.text: George Washington was a victor at this Revolutionary War battle on Christmas Day, in which his troops were able to take the namesake town after crossing the Delaware.
swap.clue: There is no historical evidence that one side got drunk the night before this battle, although more than one thousand Hessians were surprised and captured by the Revolutionary Army at this battle.

question.leadin: The epitaph of the "Boot Monument" commemorates this man's actions but does not name him.
question.text: Name this American general who defected to the British army even after he contributed to a decisive American victory at Saratoga.
question.clue: His most famous action was triggered when he was passed over for a promotion by the Continental Congress and was accused of malfeasance by other officers.

swap.leadin: After leading a rebellion in his home country, this nobleman left for the American colonies, where he participated in the revolution.
swap.text: Name this commander who was mortally wounded during a charge at the Battle of Savannah. He led a series of important military reforms alongside Michael Kovats.
swap.clue: With Michael Kovats, this Eastern European nobleman reformed the American cavalry during the Revolutionary War.

question.text: Hamilton's animosity towards Burr began when Burr defeated this man, Hamilton's father-in-law, in a Senate race in 1791. This man was acquitted of charges of incompetence at a 1779 court martial after being relieved of his command and replaced by Horatio Gates.
question.clue: This man, Hamilton's father-in-law, was a wealthy New York aristocrat of Dutch descent. He planned the 1775 invasion of Quebec and the Saratoga Campaign, but was forced out of his offices before each could begin.

swap.text: After chasing the Hannah, this ship commanded by William Dudington was set afire in 1763 off Rhode Island while attempting to enforce the Stamp Act.
swap.clue: Governor Joseph Wanton was responsible for prosecuting the men responsible for this event.

question.text: In 1765, parliament angered American colonists even more with this act that created a direct tax on all printed matter bought and sold in the colonies.
question.clue: This 1765 parliamentary act that taxed printed materials in the American colonies by requiring them to have the namesake official imprint.

swap.leadin: Identify the following American commanders in the Revolutionary War.
swap.text: This general took over for Gates and managed to weaken the British forces at such engagements as Guilford Court House and Eutaw Springs.
swap.clue: He appointed John Cox and Charles Pettit as assistants in a role in which he replaced Thomas Mifflin, that of Quartermaster General.

question.text: The force that put down the Whiskey rebellion was lead by Washington, Hamilton, and this Revolutionary War hero, who was also the father of the leader of the Confederate forces in the Civil War.
question.answerHtml: Henry “Lighthorse Harry” Lee III (prompt on partial, “H Lee” or “Lighthorse Harry” is needed)
question.clue: This Revolutionary War military figure and ninth governor of Virginia whose son would later lead the Confederate forces. He was nicknamed for his prowess as a cavalry officer.

swap.leadin: "Remember the ladies" by answering the following about women from early American history.
swap.text: A woman from this family, Mercy Warren, advocated for a Bill of Rights in her Observations on the New Constitution. Her brother from this family, James, coined the phrase "taxation without representation is tyranny."
swap.clue: A woman from this family married James Warren and was the first woman to write a history of the American Revolution.

question.leadin: Samuel Huntington succeeded John Jay as president of the Congress established by this agreement, and he spent most of his time pleading with the states for additional funding.
question.text: Name this agreement ratified in 1781 that established the 13 founding states into the United States.
question.answer: Articles of Confederation and Perpetual Union
question.clue: Another provision mandated that all military posts below general be selected by the states.

swap.leadin: Name some people who participated in the southern theatre of the American Revolutionary War.
swap.text: This commander's surprise attack on a British camp at the Battle of Black Mingo was given away by the sound of his horses crossing a wooden bridge, but he still eluded capture by Banastre Tarleton for the duration of the war.
swap.clue: This man commanded the right flank of Nathaniel Green's army at the Battle of Eutaw Springs after leading many raids against British troops stationed between the Pee Dee and Stanee Rivers, preventing full British control of South Carolina.

question.text: In Paris, Beaumarchais and Silas Deane encouraged this Scottish mercenary's plan to sabotage the Royal Navy dockyards in Portsmouth and Bristol by blowing them up, using flammable liquids obtained from his profession.
question.answerHtml: John the Painter [or James Aitken or Johnny Aitken; prompt on John or James]

swap.leadin: While working for the Culper Ring, Elizabeth Burgin helped save hundreds of people from these places because women were the only people able to visit them.
swap.text: Name these places that the British hulked near New York City. A Martyrs' Monument in Fort Greene Park honors more than 11,000 Americans who died in these places during the Revolutionary War.
swap.answerHtml: prison ships [prompt on prisons by asking “in what structures?”; prompt on ships by asking “serving what purpose?”]

question.text: St. Leger and Brant were deterred by their unsuccessful siege of this New York fort, which came to an end when they were chased off by Benedict Arnold. This fort also named two treaties between the colonists and the Iroquois in 1768 and 1784.
question.clue: A problem for Burgoyne was the inability of Barry St. Leger's force to take this fort in the Mohawk River Valley, which the British unsuccessfully besieged in August 1777.

swap.leadin: The Confederation Congress appointed him to replace Benjamin Lincoln in 1785, and four years later he became the only Confederation official to stay in the same position under the Constitution. FTPE.
swap.text: Name this famously corpulent early American politician, who retired from the government in 1794 and went back to his home "Montpelier" in Maine.
swap.clue: In that role, this general led such men as du Plessis, whose troops almost single handedly repulsed a British advance at the Battle of Monmouth.
